title: BECE English Studies: Grammar & Structure - English Studies - Modal Forms
subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Select the appropriate modal verb indicating ability in the past:
"When I was young, I _____ run very fast."
questions.explain: 'Could' is the past tense form of 'can' and is used to express an ability someone possessed in the past.
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Which modal verb best completes the sentence to show strong obligation?
"You _____ wear a helmet when riding a motorcycle."
questions.explain: 'Must' is the modal verb used to indicate strong obligation or necessity, which perfectly fits a traffic law such as wearing a helmet.
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Identify the modal verb used to ask for formal permission in the following sentence:
"_____ I leave the room now, sir?"
questions.explain: 'May' is conventionally and grammatically used to request formal permission, as in 'May I?'
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Which modal verb best fits the sentence to show logical deduction (strong probability)?
"He has been working for 12 hours straight; he _____ be exhausted."
questions.explain: 'Must' is used for logical deductions when we are almost certain that something is true based on the evidence (e.g., working 12 hours straight).
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Select the modal structure used to express a criticism about a past action that did not happen:
"You _____ me that the meeting was canceled before I drove all the way here!"
questions.explain: To express regret or criticism that something was expected but did not happen in the past, we use 'should have' + past participle.
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Identify the modal verb that indicates a lack of obligation or necessity:
"You _____ bring your textbooks tomorrow; we will be doing field work."
questions.explain: 'Needn't' (need not) indicates that an action is not necessary. In contrast, 'mustn't' (must not) implies prohibition.
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Select the modal verb that expresses strong prohibition:
"You _____ disrespect your parents under any circumstances."
questions.explain: 'Mustn't' (must not) is used to indicate that something is strictly forbidden or heavily prohibited. It is much stronger than advice ('shouldn't').
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Which modal verb best fits a polite request in the context of an offer?
"_____ I get you a glass of water, sir?"
questions.explain: 'May' is widely used in polite requests or when offering a service formally.
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Choose the correct modal verb to provide moral or general advice:
"We _____ to help the poor people in our community."
questions.explain: Among the given options, only 'ought' is idiomatically followed by 'to' when giving advice. 'Must' and 'should' are followed by a bare infinitive without 'to'.
questions.subject: English Studies
